newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday on news that the central bank had ordered state banks to phase out trading on the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract slipped to 11.50 percent from 12.05 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover shrank to 7.79 million lots from 8.52 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the People's Bank of China at a meeting in Beijing early this week told state banks to stop building new positions on the repo market and phase out existing contracts.
Traders said market sentiment was hurt and many financial institutions cut their trading due to the news.
There was a new issue of an domestic A share company, Zhejiang China Light & Textile Industrial City Group Co Ltd in Shanghai today, absorbing some funds, they said.
"The new issue made some securities brokerages borrow on the repo market today but the borrowing volume was not large enough to push up the rates, with sentiment weak," one trader said.
But traders expect the repo rates to rally next week due to decreasing money supply on the market with state banks gradually withdrawing from the market.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on the same factors as the repo market, traders said.
The most active three-year note that matures in 1999 fell to 103.14 yuan from 103.28 yuan. Total volume of the eight-contract market expanded to 1.33 million lots from 766,892 lots.

The Finance Ministry has announced that a batch of 20 billion yuan two-year treasury notes will be issued starting next week. Traders said this was a negative factor as the new issue would attract funds from the existing contracts.
They expect the rates to continue to fall early next week.
